items.caption: Otago Boys’ High Schoolin historiallinen päärakennus Dunedinissa.
items.generationPrompt: Generate a brand-new square PNG asset with genuine transparent alpha. Use case: stylized-concept. A finely engraved architectural map miniature, dark sepia lines and restrained stone-colored watercolor, accurate recognizable architecture from the following researched verbal description. Subject: the 1885 main building of Otago Boys' High School, Dunedin. Symmetrical Scottish Baronial school in brown-gray stone and conspicuous creamy limestone quoins, mullions and window surrounds. A tall square central tower crowned by FOUR very tall narrow square stepped Gothic pinnacles at its corners, two foremost and two behind; these pinnacles have decorative stacked tapering ledges, not round castle turrets. Between them a low pierced parapet and a small central rounded pediment. Tower face has two vertically stacked projecting polygonal bay windows with white rectangular mullions; the upper tall oriel is topped by a small battlement balcony, above that a small rectangular six-pane window. Ground level centered arched entrance with tiny short polygonal side buttresses. Two long two-storey slate-roof wings flank the tower with small triangular dormer gables. Each wing terminates in a larger projecting gabled bay with two stacked polygonal mullioned bay windows. School, not medieval fortress. All windows and the complete tower and pinnacles visible; a few low green shrubs at base.
items.sourceQa: Actual stepped narrow Gothic corner pinnacles and stacked projecting bay windows restored; complete school and spires.

Subject: the central clock-tower frontage of Suva Government Buildings, Fiji, the actual 1930s gray stone Art Deco civic building. A broad low symmetrical two-storey facade in large pale gray rectangular blocks. A horizontal decorative frieze of repeating incised circles runs across it below a low stepped parapet. The central square tower is a tall solid masonry shaft, with only a narrow slit window, rising from the facade. Near its top is a WHITE SQUARE clock face in a BLACK SQUARE geometric frame; its black hour marks and hands are framed by angular rectilinear spokes. Immediately below clock a projecting small stone balcony/corbel with five incised circles. The top is a short stepped masonry crown, capped by a low semicircular raised stone crest, no pointed roof. Clock is square not round. Shaft is solid stone not glazed. Wings have straight dark rectangular windows; flat roofs and small square corner pavilions. Short entrance steps and one low palm near the ground, no flag.
items.sourceQa: Square clock, solid shaft, stepped round-topped crown and circular facade reliefs match actual photograph.

Subject: the REAL Bastille fortress in Paris on 14 July 1789, based on the 1790 Palloy stone model preserved at Musée Carnavalet. Elongated rectangular massive stone block, length roughly twice the short end, bounded by EIGHT large cylindrical towers: four spaced along each long side including corner towers. Show one long side with all four cylindrical tower bulges clearly visible, and part of the shorter end in three-quarter perspective. The towers and very tall plain curtain walls have nearly the SAME height and FLAT tops with low solid parapets and narrow machicolation band; no tall spires, no conical roofs, no fantasy crenellation. The walls join the cylinders into one heavy monolithic stone prison block, sparse tiny slit windows. Small inner slate roofs may peek below parapets. At ground in front, the little Avancée gate and lowered bridge, a few tiny 1789 civilians and two modest wheeled cannons convey the event. Do not reduce the elongated eight-tower prison to a square four-tower castle. All towers, parapets, gate and base fully inside generous transparent margins.
items.sourceQa: Elongated eight-tower block with flat parapets consistent with 1790 Palloy model and 1789 painting; rear tower naturally occluded, no conical fantasy roofs.
